parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile federal layer with a hostile state layer. Entry is a universal exposure: passport markers are locked to assigned sex, 'X' markers barred, discrepancy cases tagged for refusal with possible fraud/lifetime-ineligibility referral, and trans travellers have been stranded; eight governments issued advisories. The state adds a birth-sex facilities statute covering bathrooms, shelters, dorms and prisons, sits in a 'Worst' risk tier, offers no statewide discrimination protection, and immunises religious service refusals. Federal custody mandates conversion-style treatment and immigration custody documents beatings and sexual abuse of trans detainees. Mitigants — hate-crime statute, employment ruling, 15 city ordinances, some court pushback, marriage recognition — operate below these exposures. No prosecution under the state statute is sourced, but universal exposure is rated regardless of enforcement frequency.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order and Supreme Court clearance bar self-selected markers; 'X' stopped Feb 2025. Cables instruct refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and permit fraud/lifetime-ineligibility referral; trans travellers report passports confiscated or blocked, stranded abroad; detentions of neighbouring-country trans citizens prompted advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing 'X' passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements with limited waivers and is never automatic; civil-liberties suit pending in national courts.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch → officer doubt → refusal or fraud referral → possible detention, entering custody placement regimes documented below.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style mandates (hair cutting, hormone removal, substituted psychiatric drugs) from 2026; prison population counts suppressed from 2025. Trans men in immigration custody report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse. State facilities statute expressly reaches prisons; a trans woman was held 24 hours in a men's ward after a restroom arrest in a neighbouring jurisdiction.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Prison EO rescission litigation and general habeas routes exist in principle; no documented visitor detention under the state statute.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or document investigation can escalate into federal custody where the conversion-style and placement policies apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State statute defines only male/female and covers bathrooms, locker rooms, shelters, rape-crisis centres, dormitories and prisons — a universal exposure from a rest stop onward. Nationally, 19+ state/provinces ban identity-congruent facility use in government buildings, 4 criminalise it, and one arrest under such a law is documented (trespass, 60-day misdemeanor). State ranked 'Worst', below four 'Do Not Travel' units.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Genital-examination language struck before signing; trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to depart; 29 state/provinces have no mapped ban; no prosecution under this state's statute is sourced.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal government-building ban and state statute combine so no public-facility tier is reliably safe once outed.

care_services.exposure: State's adult insurance exclusion upheld by a national appeals court in 2026; minors' care banned with narrow exception; DOJ subpoenaed 'over 20' hospitals for under-19 patient records; federal funding freezes and proposed insurance bars. Emergency ward placement congruent with identity is not documented.
care_services.protection: 1997 insurance ban was ruled unconstitutional in 2022 (later overturned at appeals level); challenge argued Dec 2025 remains pending; LGBTQ youth line services shut July 2025.
care_services.interaction: Hospital record subpoenas raise outing probability for anyone entering the care system, including visitors seeking emergency treatment.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Governor publicly frames single-sex spaces as women-only; EOs call care 'mutilation' and direct investigation of 'gender ideology'; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for identification and neutralisation; advocates compare trajectory to early genocide stages; 66% public support for assigned-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward guidance does not list 'radical gender ideology' as a reward criterion; strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; orders partly enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both the probability of challenge in facilities and the severity of any resulting encounter.

minors_guardians.exposure: EO directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; state bill would force immediate outing of trans students to parents (both houses passed, final status unresolved); minors' care banned; DOJ subpoenas under-19 medical records.
minors_guardians.protection: Student-outing bill unsigned as far as sourced; marriage and adoption rights for same-sex couples recognised; two cities ban conversion therapy.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling with a trans minor combines school/outing rhetoric, record subpoenas and facility bans; a hospital or complaint could expose the child.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity, but only 23 state/provinces add bias statutes and this state has no statewide discrimination protection; 2023 religious-refusal statute lets businesses deny service with qualified immunity; incident rates against visitors are not sourced.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime law and 2020 employment ruling operate; 15 city ordinances cover public accommodations; no organised targeting of visitors documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Service refusal plus facility exclusion leaves a visitor limited recourse while street-level violence frequency remains undocumented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Multiple provisions in motion: athletics ban, insurance challenge, ordinance-nullification and outing bills unresolved; equality-map page 404s; enforcement of the state facilities statute and religious-refusal statute against visitors not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: A national appeals court struck the athletics ban; courts have enjoined several federal orders; legal-aid FAQ and equality maps provide practical guidance.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Churning litigation means exposure varies by travel date; pending cases are open questions, not documented harms or guarantees.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.35-A, this regime imposes birth-sex facility access backed by courts and rejected or unworkable complaints, with no offence of being trans and polite everyday commerce. It rates lower because it adds a federal document/entry regime with fraud-referral exposure, documented custody conversion mandates and immigration-custody abuse, and explicit official threat-framing absent from Veluna.

Higher than 0.45-D: Veleda's worst feature is transport searches with acknowledged-but-unremedied violations. Here the exposures are broader — entry document refusal with lifetime-ineligibility possibility, statewide facilities statute reaching shelters and prisons, custody abuse — and the state sits in a 'Worst' tier, so this sits below that elevated band.

Higher than 0.25-D: Savorek combines a universal ward rule with recurrent police stops and extortion. Here no police sweeps, extortion, or arrests under the facilities statute are sourced, and working mitigants (federal hate-crime law, employment protection, 15 city ordinances, partly enjoining courts) exist — the exposures are legal and institutional rather than daily policing.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a two-level operative system that compounds rather than offsets: federal document and entry rules manufacture discovery (marker refusal, fraud referral, detention), and once discovered the state's birth-sex facilities statute and federal government-building ban govern every restroom, shelter and dormitory, while custody and immigration detention carry documented conversion mandates, beatings and sexual abuse. Official framing and a permissive religious-refusal statute leave service denial lawful with immunity. Protections — hate-crime law, employment ruling, city ordinances, enjoining courts, marriage recognition — are real but operate beneath these exposures and do not reach entry or facilities. Litigation churn adds uncertainty, not safety. The rating reflects tier-1 and tier-2 exposures with inadequate remedy, tempered by unenforced state provisions and functioning but partial federal courts.
